manifest.name: dsh-user-profile
manifest.description: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives you an editable local display profile (name + avatar) and a custom sidebar brand (product name + logo). DSH 插件：自定义用户名、头像与品牌。
manifest.author: xbbkok

bundle.text:
# dsh-user-profile — bundle patch
#
# This file is the `dsh.bundle.patch` layer of the published package. Installing
# through the official CLI:
#
#   dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-user-profile
#
# makes `dsh` append `dsh-user-profile` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`
# and merge THIS patch: one `insert` of the plugin row. No profile file edits
# needed — one command installs and mounts.
#
# Manual mount (development, or a checkout): point the same row id at the
# package entry instead. The profile patch layer is applied after the bundle
# layers and wins per row id, so it overrides this insert rather than adding a
# second one:
#
#   - insert:
#       - id: dsh-user-profile
#         name: 'file:///C:/path/to/dsh-user-profile/lib/index.js'
#
# Do not mount the package twice under two different ids: the host half owns the
# `/user-profile` route and a second instance would collide on it.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-user-profile
      name: 'dsh-user-profile'

readme.text: <div align="center">

**Your own name, avatar and brand, inside DeepSeek Harness.**

Set a username and avatar in **Settings → Profile**, or replace the product name and logo in **Settings → Brand**; both show up immediately in the sidebar.

*A local display profile for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).*

[](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [](./LICENSE) [](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [](https://github.com/xbbkok/dsh-user-profile/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](https://github.com/xbbkok/dsh-user-profile/releases) [中文](./README.zh.md) · **English** ---

The account area at the bottom-left of DSH renders the **DeepSeek Platform account** — read-only — and degrades to a generic "More" button when nobody is signed in. The top-left corner is a fixed product wordmark. Neither is yours to change.

**dsh-user-profile** fills both gaps: a name and avatar stored locally and overlaid on the account control, and an optional product name and logo that replace the sidebar brand. The account menu (settings / feedback / sign out) keeps working; only the face changes.

| | |
|---|---|
| 🪪 **Username** | Up to 32 characters, any script; leave it empty for the default |
| 🖼️ **Avatar** | PNG / JPG / WebP, center-cropped and downscaled to 192×192 |
| 🏷️ **Brand** | Product name (≤ 32 characters) and a logo for the top-left corner |
| 👀 **Live preview** | See the result while editing; the sidebar updates on save |
| 🔄 **Reversible** | Reset clears the profile and the brand restores the shipped wordmark |
| 🌐 **Localized** | Follows the DSH language setting (中文 / English) |
| 💾 **Local only** | Nothing uploaded or synced; it lives under your own `~/.dsh` |

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the official CLI also mounts the plugin row:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:xbbkok/dsh-user-profile
```

Use `desktop` instead of `web` on the desktop app, then reopen DSH.

Append an `insert` entry to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. The loader uses `import()`, so the specifier **must be a `file://` URL** — a bare Windows path fails silently:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-user-profile
      name: 'file:///C:/path/to/dsh-user-profile/lib/index.js'
```

Profile patch locations:

| Build | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop | `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml` |
| Web | `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\web\cordis.patch.yml` |
The row is keyed by id, so a later bundle install overrides the same row instead of mounting a second copy.

1. Sidebar account chip → **Settings** (`Ctrl+Alt+,`).
2. **Profile**: set a name, pick an image, press **Save**.
3. **Brand**: type a product name, upload a logo, press **Save**.
4. **Reset** in either page clears that piece and restores the shipped look.

```
%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\plugins-data\dsh-user-profile\profile.json
```

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "name": "Ada",
  "avatar": "data:image/png;base64,…",

`heartbeat.txt` in the same directory is rewritten on every host mount, so "did it load?" is a fact you can check.

The avatar is a 192×192 PNG data URL (usually 10–40 KB); the brand logo is 96×96. Both are cropped and compressed in the browser — the original file never touches disk.

The host half registers two methods on the DSH web server (same origin as the GUI):

| Method | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/user-profile` | `{ ok, profile, storagePath, capabilities }` |
| `POST` | `/user-profile` | Body `{ name?, avatar?, brand?: { name?, icon? } }`; omitted fields keep their value, `null` clears the image |

Validation: names are limited to 32 code points with control characters stripped; avatars and logos accept only PNG/JPEG/WebP `data:` URLs (**SVG is rejected** — it is executable markup, not a picture) and a byte cap; writes carrying an `Origin` that does not match the local host get a 403, so another web page cannot rewrite the profile cross-site.
`capabilities.brand` tells the client that this host half understands `brand`; a page served by an older host half shows a "restart DSH" note instead of losing an edit.

One package, two halves, like the other DSH UI plugins:

- **`lib/index.js` (host / Node)** — owns `/user-profile`: validation, atomic write (temp file + rename), heartbeat. No third-party runtime dependencies.
- **`lib/client.js` (browser)** — registers two settings sections through `ctx.slots.register({ name: 'settings.section', … })`, claims the brand slots, and overlays the avatar and name on the account trigger `button[data-signed-out]`.

Deliberate choices:

- **The brand uses the official slots.** `sidebar.brand.mark` and `sidebar.brand.name` are single slots: registrations at different priorities coexist and the lowest priority renders. The plugin claims both at priority `-1` and renders the shipped `FishLogo` / `BrandWordmark` whenever nothing custom is set, so an unconfigured install is pixel-identical to stock and clearing the brand restores it with no teardown.
- **No forking of someone else's component.** The account button belongs to `dsh-client-ui-settings-account`; editing that package would be fragile and would be overwritten by updates. The bundle decorates the DOM instead: it records each native child's `display`, hides it, inserts its own avatar and label, and restores everything when the profile is cleared. A `MutationObserver` re-applies after React re-renders, and every write is idempotent so the observer cannot feed itself (covered by a test).
- **Failures stay inside.** A missing web server, an unwritable directory or a failing route registration produce a warning, never a broken plugin tree.
- **Language follows the app.** Dictionaries go through `ctx.locale.register('user-profile', { zh, en })` and are read through

- DSH **0.2.x** (`@deepseek-ai/dsh >= 0.1.2-rc.1`), desktop and web builds.
- Uses the `settings.section` slot, the `sidebar.brand.mark` / `sidebar.brand.name` slots (priority shadowing), and the `data-signed-out` attribute of the account trigger; all are stable since 0.1.x.
- Display only: sign-in, billing and model calls are untouched.

- It changes the **displayed** profile and brand, not the DeepSeek Platform account.
- The profile is per machine; it does not sync across devices.
- The brand replaces the expanded wordmark; the collapsed rail keeps showing the mark slot, which is where a custom logo also appears.
- If a future DSH build renames `button[data-signed-out]`, the account-chip overlay silently stops applying (the settings pages keep working).
- The account-chip overlay is DOM decoration on a component owned by another package, not an official slot.

```bash
npm install   # jsdom only, for running the browser half without a GUI
npm test
```

27 checks: host validation, atomic persistence, the HTTP handler (GET / POST / brand merge and reset / malformed JSON / over-long name / SVG disguise / cross-origin write / wrong method), the 1.0.0 document upgrade, bundle loading, slot registrations with localized labels, brand slots at priority `-1` with shipped fallbacks, chip overlay and exact restoration, collapsed rail, observer settling.
Editing `lib/client.js` hot-swaps in the page; editing `lib/index.js` needs a DSH restart to re-import.
Remove the `dsh-user-profile` row from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (or drop it from `dsh.profile.bundles`), delete `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\plugins-data\dsh-user-profile\`, and refresh.
